::: {#exm-logistic-odds-interval}

#### How little six patients tell us

The two groups of @exm-logistic-regression sit two units apart on the $\predvar$ scale, so the odds ratio between them is $e^{2 \coef{1}}$.

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# fitted group odds ratio, and its interval: exponentiate twice the slope
wf_group_or_hat <- exp(2 * wf_slope)
wf_group_or <- exp(2 * wf_ci)
c(estimate = wf_group_or_hat, lower = wf_group_or[1], upper = wf_group_or[2])
```

The fitted odds of recovery in the treatment group are $`r round(wf_group_or_hat, 2)`$ times those in the control group,
with interval $(`r round(wf_group_or[1], 2)`, `r round(wf_group_or[2], 1)`)$.
The interval runs from a strong harm to a large benefit.
Its width shows how little information six observations carry about the slope.

:::
